items.question: What is Difinery?
answer: Difinery™ is a New York City fine jewelry brand making engagement rings, wedding bands, necklaces, bracelets and earrings in 14k 100% recycled solid gold set with lab-grown diamonds. Every piece is made to order in the New York Diamond District, stamped with our recycled heart hallmark, priced transparently, and sold without discounts, sales or seasonal markdowns.

items.question: Where is Difinery jewelry made?
answer: Every Difinery piece is designed and made in New York City, in the Diamond District. Our recycled gold is cast by our SCS certified casting partner here in New York, and the design, stone setting, hand finishing, polishing and quality control all happen here too. Two things come from abroad: our diamonds, which are all sourced through Belgium, and some findings such as clasps and posts. Our canvas boxes are made in Colombia. We would rather tell you exactly what comes from where than hide behind a badge.

items.question: Why are some styles not in the collection?
answer: Because making them here would put them at a price we are not willing to charge. A diamond tennis bracelet is the clearest example: the hand setting labor alone, done in New York, pushes it well past what we think is fair for that piece. We could import one and put our name on it. We would rather leave the gap. If a style you want is missing, ask us. Sometimes we can make it as a custom piece, and sometimes the honest answer is that someone else should make it for you.

items.question: What makes Difinery different from other lab-grown diamond brands?
answer: Five things. Every piece is 14k 100% recycled solid gold, certified by SCS Global Services and stamped with our recycled heart hallmark. Our white gold is natural and never rhodium plated, so there is no coating to wear off. We make to order in New York rather than holding stock or drop shipping from a catalogue. We publish transparent pricing and never run sales, discounts or countdown timers. And our warranty follows the person wearing the piece, so a gift is covered the moment it is opened.

items.question: How much does Difinery jewelry cost?
answer: Most of our pieces range from about $500 to $3,000, with options above and below that depending on the design, diamond size and customization. Engagement rings are priced by center stone size, and custom and bridal pieces are quoted individually. Every product page shows the full price with no add on fees, and the price you see is the price you pay.

items.question: Why doesn't Difinery run sales or discounts?
answer: Because a price that drops every few weeks was never the real price. We set one honest price based on materials, labor and a fair margin, and we hold it. No seasonal markdowns, no flash sales, no manufactured urgency. If you buy in March or in November, you pay the same.

items.question: Is Difinery a real jewelry brand, and is it safe to buy from?
answer: Yes. Difinery is a US based fine jewelry company that designs and makes its pieces in the New York Diamond District. Our gold is certified 100% recycled by SCS Global Services, our center diamonds ship with an IGI grading report, every piece is hallmarked 14K and carries a one year warranty, and collection pieces have a 30 day return window. Every order ships with tracking and requires a signature on delivery. Payments run through Shopify with standard buyer protections, and you can reach an actual person by email or by phone before you spend anything.

items.question: Who is Difinery for?
answer: Anyone buying fine jewelry they intend to actually wear. Our customers tend to be people who want real gold and real diamonds, care where the materials come from, and would rather understand what they are paying for than be sold to.

items.question: Who is behind Difinery?
answer: Difinery was founded in New York by three partners. Victoria Shalamoff is our brand director and the eye behind our designs and style. Albert Kimyagarov is a diamond expert and Diamond District veteran who leads production, from casting to the final polish. Marko Tatarac leads branding, marketing and operations. Every piece is designed by our team and made by hand in the New York Diamond District.

items.question: Does Difinery give back?
answer: Yes. Difinery is a member of 1% for the Planet, so 1% of every sale goes to charity, and you choose where it goes. When you add a piece to your cart, you can pick from several partner organizations, and we direct your share there.

items.question: Do you have a showroom or store I can visit?
answer: Yes. Our showroom is at 2 W 45th Street, Suite 1100, New York, NY 10036, open by appointment Monday to Friday. Book a time on our website or call us at +1 (212) 470-3049 and we will confirm within 24 hours. Can't make it in person? We also offer virtual consultations by video.

items.question: What is fine jewelry?
answer: Fine jewelry is made with precious metals such as solid gold or platinum and with genuine gemstones, including diamonds. It is built to last and to be worn for years. Unlike fashion jewelry, fine jewelry is defined not by appearance alone but by the quality of its materials, its construction and its craftsmanship.

items.question: What materials does Difinery use?
answer: Difinery jewelry is made with 14k 100% recycled solid gold, certified by SCS Global Services, and lab-grown diamonds. Our packaging uses recyclable materials and a canvas jewelry box designed to be kept rather than thrown away.

items.question: Do you offer gemstones other than diamonds, like sapphires or emeralds?
answer: No. Difinery works with lab-grown diamonds, and colored gemstones are not part of the collection. The one exception is custom work: if you bring us a natural diamond of your own, such as a family stone or one bought on the secondary market, we can set it in a custom Difinery design.

items.question: What certifications back up your recycled gold and lab-grown diamond claims?
answer: Our gold is certified 100% recycled by SCS Global Services, an independent third party certifier, through our New York casting partner, and the certificate is available on request. Our diamonds are all sourced through Belgium. Our diamonds are grown in a laboratory, and every center stone of one carat and above ships with a grading report from IGI, the International Gemological Institute, which documents its laboratory grown origin along with its cut, color, clarity and carat weight.

items.question: What does the recycled heart stamp on my Difinery piece mean?
answer: It is our promise in metal. Every Difinery piece is stamped inside with three marks: 14K, which certifies the gold content, a small recycled heart, which shows the gold is 100% recycled, and the Difinery maker's mark. The heart means no newly mined gold went into your piece, and it stays with the piece for life.

items.question: How does Difinery approach sustainability?
answer: We focus on the parts we can actually control and measure. Our gold is 100% recycled, which means no newly mined material enters our supply. Our diamonds are grown in a laboratory rather than extracted. We make to order, so we do not overproduce or write off unsold stock. Our packaging is recyclable and designed to be reused. We finish everything in New York, which keeps our production close and traceable. We are careful not to claim that any jewelry is impact free, because making anything has a footprint. What we can tell you is exactly what our materials are and where the work happens.

items.question: What happens to the leftover gold in your workshop?
answer: Nothing goes to waste. The gold left over at our bench is kept and used for resizing and repairing Difinery pieces, so the extra metal from one piece goes into keeping another one in shape.

items.question: Are lab-grown diamonds better for the environment than mined diamonds?
answer: Growing a diamond in a laboratory avoids the land disturbance and material displacement involved in mining, and it removes the sourcing questions that come with mined stones. The energy used to grow diamonds varies by producer and by the electricity grid behind them, so the honest answer is that the footprint depends on the grower rather than on the category. We prefer to tell you what we do rather than to publish a blanket environmental claim.

items.question: Does Difinery gold contain nickel?
answer: Our 14k yellow gold contains no nickel. It is gold, silver, copper and zinc. Our 14k white gold does contain nickel, which is the standard whitening metal in white gold, alongside gold, zinc and copper. Every one of those alloy metals is recycled. If you know you react to nickel, choose yellow or rose gold, and if you are unsure, contact us before ordering and we will tell you exactly what is in the piece you are looking at.

items.question: What exactly is in Difinery's gold?
answer: All Difinery gold is 100% recycled, conflict free and responsibly sourced, and does not directly or indirectly finance armed groups. 14k yellow gold is gold, silver, copper and zinc. 14k white gold is gold, zinc, copper and nickel. 14k rose gold uses a higher ratio of copper for its pink tone. All three are at least 58.5% pure gold, with the remaining 41.5% made up of the alloy metals that give the gold its strength and its color. All of those alloy metals are recycled as well.

items.question: Is Difinery jewelry safe for sensitive skin?
answer: Solid 14k gold is a common choice for people who react to plated or base metal jewelry, because there is no coating to wear through and no base metal underneath. One thing to know: our white gold alloy contains nickel, which is the most common cause of metal sensitivity, while our yellow and rose gold do not. If you react to nickel, choose yellow or rose. If you are unsure, contact us before ordering and we will tell you exactly what is in the alloy so you can decide for yourself.

items.question: Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value over time?
answer: Fine jewelry, lab-grown or mined, is not an investment product, and we would not sell it to you as one. Resale value for any diamond depends heavily on the piece, the buyer and where it is sold, and lab-grown diamond prices have been falling as production scales. What we can promise is quality and fair pricing: a lab-grown diamond is a real diamond with the same physical, optical and chemical properties as a mined one, and our center diamonds ship with an independent grading report documenting their specifications.

items.question: What does 14k recycled solid gold mean?
answer: Every gram has had a past life. It was melted down, refined and reborn into something new, with no new mining behind it. Gold's properties do not change when it is recycled, so you get the same quality, purity and longevity as freshly mined 14k. It needs no special care, just occasional polishing to keep it bright.

items.question: What is the difference between 14k and 18k gold?
answer: Karat measures how much pure gold is in the metal. 14k is 58.5% pure gold, 18k is 75%. 14k is more resistant to scratches and dents, which makes it the better choice for everyday wear. 18k is slightly purer and warmer in color but softer. Difinery uses 14k because it holds up to real life.

items.question: What is the difference between karat and carat?
answer: Karat with a K measures gold purity, so 14k means 58.5% pure gold blended with strengthening metals. Carat with a C measures the weight of a diamond or gemstone, where one carat equals 0.2 grams.

items.question: Is recycled gold lower quality than newly mined gold?
answer: No. Refined recycled gold is chemically and structurally identical to newly mined gold of the same karat. Recycled refers only to where the metal came from, not to what it is. Difinery's 14k recycled gold has the same durability, purity and longevity as freshly mined 14k.

items.question: Why does Difinery use recycled gold instead of newly mined gold?
answer: Because there is already an enormous amount of gold above ground, and reusing it means no new mining is needed to make your ring. Recycled gold is chemically identical to newly mined gold, so there is no trade off in quality, only in origin.

items.question: Where does Difinery's recycled gold come from?
answer: From gold that has already been mined and used. Recycled gold is recovered from sources such as old jewelry, dental gold and industrial and electronic scrap, then sent to a refinery where it is melted and purified back to pure gold, identical to newly mined gold. It is then alloyed to 14k with recycled silver, copper, zinc and, for white gold, nickel. Our casting partner, here in the New York Diamond District, is certified by SCS Global Services, so every piece we make is 100% recycled gold and no newly mined gold enters our supply.

items.question: How is a Difinery piece made?
answer: By hand, in about five business days, entirely in the New York Diamond District. Every piece goes through ten steps:

list: **Design.** Each piece starts as a precise 3D design.
**3D printing.** The design is printed as a pattern accurate to fractions of a millimeter.
**Casting.** Our SCS certified casting partner in New York casts the pattern in 100% recycled 14k gold, using the lost wax technique jewelers have relied on for centuries.
**Pre finishing.** The raw casting is cleaned up and shaped by hand.
**Tumbling.** The piece is tumbled to harden and smooth the metal.
**Stone seat preparation.** The jeweler cuts the exact seat each diamond will sit in.
**Pre polish.** The surfaces are polished before any stone goes in.
**Stone setting.** Each diamond is set by hand, one at a time, under magnification.
**Final polish.** The finished piece is polished to its final shine.
**Quality check and finishing.** Every piece is inspected, hallmarked with our 14K, recycled heart and maker's marks, and packed for you.

items.question: Can I wear 14k solid gold every day?
answer: Yes. 14k solid gold is one of the most durable choices for everyday wear. Its blend of pure gold and strengthening metals resists scratches and dents better than higher karat gold.

items.question: Will my gold jewelry tarnish?
answer: No. Solid 14k gold does not tarnish, flake or fade the way plated or filled metals do. Over time it may pick up light surface scratches and a soft patina from daily wear, which a professional polish removes.

items.question: Why is there a dark mark on my skin where I wear my ring?
answer: It happens now and then, and it is usually nothing to worry about. Even solid gold contains small amounts of other metals, like silver and copper, for strength. For some people, everyday things like body chemistry, lotions, sanitizer or a change in medication can react with those metals and leave a light gray or black mark on the skin. It is not an allergic reaction, which usually shows up as redness, itching or a rash, and it washes off with soap and water. Keeping the ring clean and dry usually stops it. If it keeps happening, some people find a different gold color works better for them, and we are always happy to clean your piece or talk through options.

items.question: What is the difference between yellow, white and rose gold?
answer: All three start from the same recycled 14k gold, and the alloy blended in gives each its color. Yellow gold is blended with silver, copper and zinc for a classic warm glow. Rose gold uses a higher ratio of copper for its pink tone. White gold is blended with zinc, copper and nickel for a soft, natural white. All three are at least 58.5% pure gold and share the same durability and recycled origin. The difference is color, not quality, with one practical note: only the white gold contains nickel.

items.question: Do you offer white gold and rose gold, or only yellow?
answer: Every Difinery piece is available in yellow gold and white gold, and many designs also come in rose gold. Each product page shows the colors available for that piece.

items.question: Does the gold color affect the quality or the price?
answer: No. Yellow, white and rose gold are all 14k, all 100% recycled, and all priced the same. Choose the color you like.

items.question: Which gold color should I choose?
answer: Choose the one that sits naturally with what you already wear. Yellow gold reads warm and classic, white gold reads soft and modern, rose gold reads soft and romantic. All three are the same purity and durability, so there is no right answer, only your answer. Each product page shows which colors that piece comes in.

items.question: Is Difinery white gold rhodium plated?
answer: No. Our 14k white gold is left natural, with no rhodium plating. That gives it a soft, slightly warm white tone that stays the same over time, so it never needs replating the way plated white gold does. It is the same metal all the way through, which fits our focus on pieces built to last.

items.question: Why isn't Difinery white gold rhodium plated like most white gold?
answer: Because plating wears off. Most 14k white gold is coated with rhodium for a bright, icy finish, and that coating thins with daily wear, exposing a warmer metal underneath and needing to be redone every year or two. We would rather give you a color that is honest from the start and does not change. What you see on day one is what you will see in ten years.

items.question: What is the difference between solid gold, gold filled and gold plated jewelry?
answer: Solid gold is gold all the way through. Gold filled jewelry has a thick layer of gold mechanically bonded to a base metal core. Gold plated jewelry, including vermeil, has only a thin layer of gold applied over a base metal, which wears off over time. Difinery pieces are 100% solid 14k gold, never filled or plated, which is why they do not flake, fade or need replating.

items.question: What is gold vermeil, and does Difinery use it?
answer: Gold vermeil is sterling silver with a layer of gold plating over it, usually thicker than standard plating but still a plating rather than solid gold. Difinery does not use vermeil. Every piece is solid 14k gold.

items.question: How can I tell if a piece is solid gold and not plated?
answer: Solid gold jewelry is stamped with a hallmark showing its karat, for example 14K. It also behaves differently over time: it will not flake, discolor or reveal a different metal underneath with normal wear, while plated pieces thin out and eventually show the base metal beneath.

items.question: Are Difinery pieces hallmarked?
answer: Yes. Every piece is stamped inside with three marks: 14K to certify the gold content, our recycled heart to show it is made from recycled gold, and our Difinery maker's mark. You can also add a personal engraving of your own, such as initials, a date or a short message, alongside the hallmark.

items.question: Can I trade in my old jewelry with Difinery?
answer: Yes, for any Difinery piece. Trade it in for store credit toward something new. Send us photos and any certificates that came with it, then ship it to us with an insured, trackable service at your cost. Our team evaluates it in person and sends you a store credit offer. We do not accept jewelry from other brands as trade ins. If you have an old piece or a diamond of your own that you would like to wear differently, we can rework it into a custom Difinery design instead.

items.question: What is a lab-grown diamond?
answer: A lab-grown diamond is a real diamond created in a controlled laboratory environment rather than formed underground. It has the same carbon crystal structure, the same hardness and the same optical properties as a mined diamond. The only difference is where it came from.

items.question: Are lab-grown diamonds real diamonds?
answer: Yes. A lab-grown diamond is a diamond. It is chemically, physically and optically the same material as a mined diamond, and it is graded on the same standards by the same laboratories. It is not a simulant like cubic zirconia or moissanite, which are different materials entirely. Every Difinery diamond is clearly identified as laboratory grown on its grading report and on the product page.

items.question: What is the difference between a lab-grown diamond and a mined diamond?
answer: They are physically, chemically and optically identical. The difference is origin and timeline. Mined diamonds formed underground over an extremely long period and were extracted. Lab-grown diamonds are created in a controlled environment in roughly 6 to 12 weeks.

items.question: Are lab-grown diamonds cheaper than mined diamonds?
answer: Yes, usually significantly. A lab-grown diamond typically costs a fraction of a comparable mined diamond of the same carat weight, color and clarity, because the supply chain is shorter and the stone can be produced to order. Practically, that means you can choose a larger or higher graded stone for the same budget.

items.question: Do lab-grown diamonds pass a diamond tester?
answer: Yes. Standard thermal and electrical diamond testers read lab-grown diamonds as diamonds, because that is what they are. Distinguishing lab-grown from mined requires specialized laboratory equipment, which is why our center diamonds ship with a grading report stating their laboratory grown origin.

items.question: Can a jeweler tell the difference between a lab-grown and a mined diamond?
answer: Not by eye. They look identical, wear identically and test as diamond. Origin is determined with specialized laboratory screening equipment, and reputable labs can identify it reliably. We never leave that to guesswork: every Difinery diamond is disclosed as laboratory grown in writing, on the product page and on its grading report.

items.question: Will a lab-grown diamond cloud, fade or lose its sparkle over time?
answer: No. A lab-grown diamond does not change, cloud or fade. It is the same material as a mined diamond and rates 10 on the Mohs hardness scale. What does change is surface film from lotion, soap and skin oil, which makes any diamond look dull. A quick clean brings the sparkle straight back.

items.question: What is the difference between CVD and HPHT diamonds?
answer: Both are methods of growing real diamonds, and Difinery uses both. CVD, or chemical vapor deposition, grows a diamond layer by layer from a carbon rich gas at relatively low pressure. HPHT, or high pressure high temperature, recreates conditions similar to those found deep in the earth. Some stones are grown with one method and refined with the other. The growth method does not by itself determine quality. What matters is the finished stone's cut, color and clarity, which is why every Difinery diamond meets the same D to F color and VVS2 to VS2 clarity standard whichever way it was grown.

items.question: Where are Difinery's diamonds grown?
answer: All of our lab-grown diamonds are sourced through Belgium, one of the world's oldest and most trusted diamond trading centers. Every stone, center or accent, meets the same D to F color and VVS2 to VS2 clarity standard.

items.question: How is a lab-grown diamond grown?
answer: It starts with a thin slice of diamond called a seed. With CVD, the seed sits in a chamber filled with carbon rich gas, and carbon atoms settle onto it layer by layer until a rough diamond forms over several weeks. With HPHT, the seed is placed in carbon under the kind of heat and pressure found deep in the earth, and the diamond crystallizes around it. Either way, the rough stone is then cut and polished by hand, exactly like a mined diamond, and graded by an independent lab.

items.question: Are lab-grown diamonds conflict free?
answer: Lab-grown diamonds are created in a laboratory, so they are not connected to mining regions or to the sourcing concerns associated with mined stones. We can tell you which laboratory produced your diamond, and its grading report documents its origin as laboratory grown.

items.question: Do lab-grown diamonds have inclusions?
answer: Yes, they can. Diamonds grown in a laboratory develop small internal characteristics just as mined diamonds do, and they are graded for clarity on the same scale. Difinery uses diamonds in the VVS2 to VS2 clarity range, which are eye clean, meaning inclusions are not visible without magnification.

items.question: What color and clarity does Difinery use?
answer: Our diamonds are D, E or F in color, which is the colorless range, and VVS2, VS1 or VS2 in clarity, which is eye clean. Center stones of one carat and above ship with an IGI grading report documenting their specifications.

items.question: Is a lab-grown diamond a good choice for an engagement ring?
answer: Yes, and it is now one of the most common choices. You get a real diamond, the same hardness and the same brilliance, with a clearer picture of where it came from and typically a much better stone for your budget. The decision comes down to what matters to you: if the origin story of a mined stone is important to you, that is a valid reason to choose one. If you want the best diamond your budget can buy, lab-grown makes that easier.

items.question: What are the 4Cs of diamond quality?
answer: Cut is the precision of the shaping and polishing, including proportions, symmetry and polish, and it is what makes a diamond sparkle. Color measures how colorless a diamond is. Clarity grades how few and how noticeable its internal characteristics are. Carat measures weight, where one carat equals 0.2 grams. A grading report documents all four.

items.question: What do the diamond color grades D to Z mean?
answer: Diamond color runs from D, completely colorless and the most valuable, to Z, noticeably tinted. Most fine jewelry uses stones in the D to J range, where any warmth is hard to see once the stone is set. Difinery uses D, E and F.

items.question: What do the diamond clarity grades FL to I3 mean?
answer: Clarity runs from Flawless, with no inclusions visible even under magnification, down to Included, where inclusions are visible to the naked eye. Most fine jewelry uses VS or SI grades, which are typically eye clean. Difinery uses VVS2, VS1 and VS2.

items.question: What does eye clean mean?
answer: It means the inclusions are not visible to the unaided eye under normal viewing. It is not an official clarity grade. A diamond can have inclusions under magnification and still look completely clean and bright when worn.

items.question: What is the difference between a diamond's cut and its shape?
answer: Shape is the outline: round, oval, pear, marquise, emerald, princess, radiant, cushion, asscher, heart. Cut is the proportions, faceting, symmetry and polish that determine how the stone handles light. Shape is what a diamond looks like. Cut is what makes it sparkle.

items.question: What diamond shapes does Difinery offer?
answer: All of them. Whether you love a classic round, an elongated oval, an emerald or a pear, or something more unusual like a marquise, radiant, cushion, princess, asscher or heart, we can source a lab-grown diamond in any shape you choose. Round returns the most light. Step cut shapes like emerald and asscher show clean, glassy flashes and reward high clarity. Elongated shapes like oval, pear and marquise tend to look larger for their carat weight. Not sure which suits you? Contact us and we will help you compare.

items.question: What is diamond fluorescence?
answer: Fluorescence is a diamond's reaction to ultraviolet light. Some diamonds emit a faint glow, usually blue, under UV sources including sunlight. In most cases it has little or no visible effect on how the diamond looks in normal lighting.

items.question: What are hearts and arrows?
answer: Hearts and arrows is a pattern found in round brilliant diamonds cut with exceptional symmetry. Viewed one way through a special scope the facets form a ring of hearts, viewed the other way they form a ring of arrows. It signals precise cutting, though it is not a formal grade on a grading report.

items.question: What is a diamond setting?
answer: A setting is the metal structure that holds a diamond in place. It affects how the stone looks, how well it is protected and how much light reaches it. Common styles include prong, bezel, pavé, channel, fishtail and halo.

items.question: What is the difference between a center diamond and accent diamonds?
answer: The center diamond is the main stone and the focal point of the piece. Accent diamonds are smaller stones set around it, along the band or into the setting, adding detail, balance and extra light without competing with the center.

items.question: What does total carat weight mean?
answer: Often written as ct. tw., total carat weight is the combined weight of every diamond in a piece, not the weight of a single stone. A ring listed at 2.10 ct. tw. might have one center stone and many accents adding up to that total.

items.question: What is the difference between a GIA and an IGI report?
answer: Both are internationally recognized diamond grading laboratories that grade on the same 4Cs standards. GIA, the Gemological Institute of America, is the long standing benchmark and is most associated with mined diamonds. IGI, the International Gemological Institute, grades the majority of the world's lab-grown diamonds. A report from either is a credible, independent assessment.

items.question: What certification comes with a Difinery diamond, and who issues it?
answer: Every center diamond of one carat and above ships with a grading report issued by IGI, the International Gemological Institute, not by us. The report documents the stone's laboratory grown origin along with its cut, color, clarity and carat weight. Smaller stones and accent diamonds are not individually certified, which is standard across the industry, and they are held to the same D to F color and VVS2 to VS2 clarity standard as everything else we set.

items.question: What is the difference between a grading report and an appraisal?
answer: A grading report describes the diamond itself: its measurements, cut, color, clarity, carat weight and origin. It is issued by an independent laboratory, and it comes with every center stone of one carat and above. An appraisal is different. It states an estimated replacement value for the finished piece, and it is the document your insurer will ask for. An appraisal is not included with your order, and we can arrange an independent third party appraisal for $100 per piece. Ask us at any time, before or after you buy.

items.question: Should I insure my jewelry?
answer: For anything you wear daily, especially an engagement ring, it is worth it. Standard homeowner or renter policies often cover jewelry only up to a low limit, so most people add a rider or a standalone jewelry policy. An independent appraisal, which we can arrange for $100, gives an insurer what it needs. We do not sell insurance and we do not receive anything for recommending it.

items.question: Can I order a custom engagement ring?
answer: Yes. Difinery offers a guided custom process. You share your idea, your preferences and any reference images, and we develop the design with you, produce a 3D rendering for your approval, then print, cast, set, hand finish, polish and quality check the finished ring in our New York atelier.

items.question: How does the custom process work, start to finish?
answer: Contact us with your idea and we respond within 24 hours. We develop the design and send you a 3D rendering to review and approve. Once you approve it, production begins and takes about 5 business days in our New York atelier, covering 3D printing, casting, stone setting, hand finishing, polishing and quality control. Shipping by USPS Priority Mail adds 2 to 3 days.

items.question: How is a custom engagement ring priced?
answer: Price depends on the design, the metal, the diamond specifications, the setting and the level of detail. We give you the full quote in writing before production begins, and it does not change afterward unless you change the design.

items.question: Are custom design deposits refundable?
answer: We take a 50% deposit to begin design work. The deposit is refundable until you approve your 3D rendering, minus a $200 design fee that covers the design time. Once you approve the rendering, we order materials and begin production, so the deposit becomes non refundable and the balance is due before your piece ships.

items.question: How many design revisions are included?
answer: Your quote includes three rounds of revisions on the 3D rendering, which is enough for almost every design. If you need more, additional rounds are $75 each, and we always tell you before anything is billable.

items.question: Can I cancel or change a custom design after I approve the rendering?
answer: Once you approve the 3D rendering, production begins immediately and materials are committed, so a custom piece cannot be cancelled, returned, exchanged or refunded after that point. Review the rendering carefully before approving: check the size, the stone specifications and every design detail. If anything is unclear, ask us. We would much rather revise a rendering than disappoint you with a finished ring.

items.question: Do custom pieces have different timelines, return rules or warranty coverage?
answer: Timelines are the same once the design is settled: about 5 business days of production after you approve the rendering, plus shipping. What comes before that, the design conversation and the rendering approval, is what makes a custom order take longer overall. Return rules are different: custom pieces cannot be returned, exchanged or refunded. Warranty coverage is identical. Custom pieces carry the same one year warranty as everything else we make.

items.question: Can you use my own gold or diamond, like a family heirloom?
answer: Yes. We can rework your old gold and reset your own diamond into a new Difinery design, so a piece with history becomes something you will actually wear. Send us photos and we will tell you what is possible and give you a written quote before anything is touched.

items.question: What if I do not know the ring size for a proposal?
answer: We will work it out together before you order. The easiest method is to borrow a ring the recipient already wears on the correct finger and hand, since sizes differ between hands. You can also print our ring size guide at 100% scale and measure that ring against it. If you are still unsure, contact us before ordering. And remember that most Difinery rings include one complimentary resizing, so a near miss is fixable.

items.question: How much should I spend on an engagement ring?
answer: Whatever amount you can spend without it hurting. The old rule about two or three months of salary was an advertising campaign, not financial advice. A better approach is to set a number you are comfortable with first, then use lab-grown diamonds and a well chosen setting to get the most ring for it. We will happily show you what a specific budget buys.

items.question: How far in advance should I order an engagement ring?
answer: For a piece from the collection, allow about two weeks from order to delivery, and more during the holiday season and spring engagement season. For a custom piece, allow three to five weeks from first conversation to delivery, since the design work and your approval come before the five days of production. If you have a date in mind, tell us and we will tell you honestly whether it is possible rather than promising and missing it.

items.question: What size diamond should I choose?
answer: There is no correct size, only the right size for the hand and the wearer. A few practical notes: elongated shapes like oval, pear and marquise look larger than round stones of the same carat weight, smaller finger sizes make any stone read bigger, and a well cut smaller stone will outshine a poorly cut larger one. If you send us the finger size and a sense of style, we will suggest a range.

items.question: What is the difference between an engagement ring and a wedding band?
answer: An engagement ring usually features a center diamond and is given at the proposal. A wedding band is exchanged at the ceremony and is traditionally simpler, either plain metal or set with smaller diamonds all the way around or partway around. Many people wear both stacked on the same finger, which is why band profile and fit matter.

items.question: Do you make matching or contoured wedding bands?
answer: Yes. We can create a band designed to sit flush against your engagement ring, whether that is a classic match, a curved contour shaped around your center stone, or something completely custom. Every band is made to order in recycled 14k gold, with bridal pricing that is highly competitive. Share your ring or your idea with us, and we will take it from there.

items.question: Can I upgrade my center diamond later?
answer: Yes. You can trade in your Difinery center diamond toward a new one, and we credit what you originally paid for it. The new center stone must cost at least twice what you paid for the original, and the original diamond must come back undamaged with its IGI report. You pay the price difference plus the labor to reset the stone.

items.question: Can I see or try on a ring before buying?
answer: Yes. Every piece is made to order, so we do not keep a full inventory, but our showroom at 2 W 45th Street has samples you can see and try on. Book an appointment and sit down with Albert Kimyagarov, our diamond expert and production lead, to talk through your idea, compare stones and settings, and get your size right. If you can't come in, we offer the same consultation by video, and we send a free printable size guide with every consultation.

items.question: How do I find my ring size?
answer: Two ways. Measure a ring that already fits you and match it to our size chart, or download our ring sizing guide, print it at 100% scale, wrap the measuring strip around your finger, mark it and read the size off the chart. If you are unsure, email support@difinery.com with photos or measurements and we will help you get it right.

items.question: What ring sizes do you offer?
answer: Sizes 4 through 12 in half size increments, so 4, 4.5, 5, 5.5 and so on. If you fall between sizes or need something outside that range, contact us and we will make the ring to your exact size.

items.question: Do you offer half sizes?
answer: Yes. Our standard size run is in half size increments.

items.question: Do you offer UK, EU or international ring sizing?
answer: Our sizes are US sizes. If you know your size in UK, EU or any other scale, just send it to us and we will convert it for you.

items.question: What should I do if I am between sizes?
answer: Consider the band width first, since wider bands fit more snugly than narrow ones, and fingers swell over the course of a day and in warm weather. Do not size down to something that feels tight. If you are unsure, contact us before ordering, and remember that most rings include one complimentary resizing.

items.question: Can my ring size change over time?
answer: Yes. Fingers change with age, weight, pregnancy, temperature, exercise and even the time of day. It is completely normal, and it is why we include resizing.

items.question: Are open rings adjustable?
answer: An open ring has a fixed opening and should not be repeatedly pulled open or squeezed closed, since that weakens the metal and distorts the shape. Choose the closest size rather than forcing an adjustment.

items.question: What necklace lengths do you offer?
answer: 16 inches, 18 inches and 20 inches. A 16 inch chain sits high on the neck, 18 inches is the most versatile and usually falls near the collarbone, and 20 inches sits lower and works well for pendants and for layering.

items.question: How do I measure my necklace length?
answer: Take a piece of string or a soft tape measure, place it around your neck where you want the necklace to sit, mark the point where it meets, then measure the length. That is your ideal chain length. If it falls between our sizes, size up rather than down.

items.question: What bracelet lengths do you offer?
answer: Bracelet lengths vary by design, so check the product page for the options on a specific piece. Measure your wrist with a soft tape measure and add about half an inch for a comfortable fit, or a little more if you prefer a looser drape.

items.question: How long will my order take?
answer: Every Difinery piece is made to order, so nothing is pre made and nothing is overproduced. Production takes about 5 business days for 3D printing, casting, stone setting, hand finishing, polishing and quality control in our New York atelier. We then ship by USPS Priority Mail, which takes 2 to 3 days, with a signature required on delivery. Most orders arrive within about 7 to 8 business days of being placed. During the holiday season and the spring engagement season, production can run longer, and we will tell you at the time of order rather than after.

items.question: Will my order arrive in time for the holidays?
answer: Every Difinery piece is made to order just for you, so we do not keep ready to ship stock. During the holiday season, production and shipping can take a little longer than usual. For delivery before Christmas, we recommend ordering by December 1. If you have a specific date in mind, contact us before you order and we will give you an honest estimate.

items.question: Where do you ship?
answer: Within the United States only at this time. International shipping is not available yet.

items.question: Will you ship internationally in the future?
answer: International expansion is on our roadmap. We are focused on serving US customers first and doing it properly. Join our email list and we will tell you when that changes.

items.question: Can you ship to a PO Box or an APO or FPO address?
answer: No. Every order requires a signature on delivery, so we do not ship to PO Boxes or to APO and FPO addresses. Please use a street address at checkout.

items.question: Is shipping free?
answer: Standard shipping is free on orders of $300 or more. Below that, the exact carrier cost is shown at checkout with nothing added on top.

items.question: How will my order arrive?
answer: Your piece ships in a plain, unbranded outer box, so nothing on the outside hints at what is inside. Open it and you will find our signature Difinery presentation box, with your piece nestled in a linen jewelry case, ready to give as a gift. Every order ships with tracking and insurance, and a signature is required on delivery so your piece never sits unattended on a doorstep. If anything happens to your package in transit, contact us right away and we will take care of it.

items.question: Is the packaging discreet if the piece is a gift or a surprise?
answer: Yes. The outer shipping box is plain and carries no jewelry branding, so a package arriving at a shared home does not give away the surprise. The shipping label carries no Difinery name either. Only the presentation box inside is branded.

items.question: Can I track my order?
answer: Yes. When your order ships you will receive a confirmation email with a tracking link. Allow up to 48 hours for tracking to activate.

items.question: What if my package is delayed, lost or damaged?
answer: Start with the tracking link in your shipping confirmation email, allowing up to 48 hours for it to activate. If your package has not arrived within the estimated window, or if it shows as delivered and you cannot find it, contact us at support@difinery.com with your order number as soon as possible and we will take it from there with the carrier. If a package arrives damaged, take photos and contact us before wearing the piece so we can review it and make it right.

items.question: What payment methods do you accept?
answer: All major credit and debit cards, including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Elo, JCB and UnionPay, plus Shop Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal. Apple Pay and Google Pay appear depending on your device. Express checkout is available for a faster one tap purchase.

items.question: Can I pay over time?
answer: Yes. Choose Shop Pay at checkout and select Shop Pay Installments to split your purchase into smaller payments, subject to approval. Your options and terms are shown before you confirm your order.

items.question: Is sales tax added to my order?
answer: Yes, calculated automatically at checkout based on your shipping address and your state's rules. The full total including tax is shown before you pay, and nothing is added afterward.

items.question: Can I cancel my order?
answer: Yes, within 24 hours of placing it, for a full refund. After that, your piece has already gone into production and the order cannot be canceled. Contact support@difinery.com with your order number as soon as possible. Custom orders follow the deposit terms agreed when your design is approved.

items.question: What is your return policy?
answer: You can return any eligible piece within 30 days of delivery for a full refund to your original payment method. To qualify, the piece must be unworn, with no scratches, damage, resizing or alterations, and it must come back in its original packaging with all certificates, grading reports and documents. Custom, engraved and resized pieces are final sale. Every return is inspected when it arrives. If a piece shows signs of wear or damage, we cannot accept it and will ship it back to you. Approved refunds are issued within 5 to 7 business days of inspection.

items.question: Who pays for return shipping?
answer: You do. Please use an insured, trackable service, since we cannot be responsible for packages lost in transit. Once we receive and approve your return, we refund the full purchase price with no restocking fees or deductions. Original shipping charges are not refundable.

items.question: Do returns extend over the holidays?
answer: Yes. Orders placed between November 1 and December 31 can be returned through January 31.

items.question: How do I start a return?
answer: Email support@difinery.com with your order number and we will send you return instructions within 24 hours.

items.question: How long does a refund take?
answer: We inspect returns within 3 to 5 business days of receiving them, and approved refunds are issued within 5 to 7 business days of inspection. Your bank may take a few more days to post the funds to your account.

items.question: Are engraved pieces returnable?
answer: No. Engraving is a permanent personalization, so an engraved piece is final sale. If you are not certain about the piece itself, order it plain first. You can always send it back to us for engraving later.

items.question: What cannot be returned?
answer: Custom pieces made to your specification, completely new designs created for you, and engraved pieces are final sale, because they are made for one person and cannot be resold. Pieces that have been worn, scratched, damaged, resized or altered are not eligible. Gift cards are not returnable. Special Collection and special order pieces can be returned for store credit rather than a refund to your original payment method, and must still be unworn, undamaged and in original packaging.
Resizing is not a return. If the only issue is fit, do not send it back for a refund, send it back to be resized.

items.question: Do you offer exchanges?
answer: We do not process direct exchanges. If you want something different, request a return on the eligible piece and place a new order. If the issue is fit rather than choice, do not return it: most rings include one complimentary resizing.

items.question: Do gift cards expire?
answer: No. Difinery gift cards never expire and carry no fees. They can be used toward any Difinery piece, are not reloadable, and cannot be redeemed for cash except where state law requires it. Treat a gift card like cash: if it is lost or stolen, contact us with your order details and we will do our best to help.

items.question: Can I wear my jewelry every day?
answer: Yes. That is what it is built for. 14k solid gold handles daily wear and does not tarnish or fade, and lab-grown diamonds are just as hard as mined ones.

items.question: Can I shower, work out or swim in my jewelry?
answer: Showering and everyday activity are fine, and plenty of people never take their pieces off. Two things to avoid where you can: chlorinated pools and saltwater, which are hard on metal over time, and heavy lifting or impact sports, where a band can be dented or a stone knocked. Damage from chemical exposure and from accidents is not covered under the warranty, so a small habit of taking a ring off at the gym pays for itself.

items.question: Should I take jewelry off before perfume, sunscreen, skincare or hair products?
answer: Yes. The oils, alcohols and polymers in those products leave a film that dulls metal and clouds stones, and they are a common cause of a dark mark on the skin under a ring. Put jewelry on last when you get ready, and take it off first at the end of the day.

items.question: How do I clean my jewelry at home?
answer: Soak the piece for a few minutes in lukewarm water with a couple of drops of mild dish soap, then gently brush around and underneath the stones with a soft toothbrush, rinse thoroughly and pat dry with a soft lint free cloth. Between cleanings, a quick wipe with a soft cloth after wearing does most of the work. Avoid harsh chemicals, bleach, and abrasive cleaners or toothpaste.

items.question: Why does my diamond look cloudy?
answer: Almost always because of a film of soap, lotion or skin oil on the underside of the stone, where light enters. It is the single most common reason a diamond looks dull, and it is fixed in five minutes with warm water, mild soap and a soft brush.

items.question: Can I use an ultrasonic cleaner at home?
answer: We would rather you did not. Ultrasonic cleaners can loosen stones in prong and pavé settings, and they can worsen an existing weakness you cannot see. Warm water and mild soap are safer at home. Every Difinery piece includes complimentary professional cleaning for 6 months, or 12 months when you subscribe through the QR code in your box, and that is the right place for a deep clean.

items.question: How should I store my jewelry?
answer: Each piece in its own dry, soft lined compartment or pouch, kept separate so pieces cannot scratch or tangle. Close clasps before storing necklaces, and keep jewelry out of humid places like bathrooms.

items.question: What should I do if a stone feels loose or a prong catches on clothing?
answer: Stop wearing the piece and contact us right away. Do not try to push the stone or the prong back yourself, because that is how a stone gets lost. Email support@difinery.com with your order number and clear photos and we will tell you whether it needs inspection or repair.

items.question: Do you offer cleaning and polishing?
answer: Yes. Every Difinery piece includes complimentary professional cleaning and polishing for 6 months after delivery. Scan the QR code inside your shipping box and subscribe, and we extend that to a full 12 months. The extension is yours once earned, whether or not you stay subscribed. It covers ultrasonic cleaning, gentle polishing and a general condition inspection, and we ship the piece back to you at no cost. Email support@difinery.com to arrange it. Once we receive the piece we complete the service within 7 to 10 business days. Structural repairs, resizing, engraving and damage repair are not part of the complimentary service.

items.question: How often should prongs, clasps and settings be inspected?
answer: For a piece you wear daily, especially an engagement ring, we recommend a professional inspection every 6 to 12 months. Prongs wear down gradually and a loose stone is far cheaper to tighten than to replace. Inspections during your complimentary cleaning period are included.

items.question: Do you offer a warranty?
answer: Yes. Every piece comes with a complimentary one year limited warranty against defects in materials and workmanship, starting on the day your order is delivered. Scan the QR code inside your shipping box to register your piece, and subscribe there to extend your complimentary cleaning from 6 to 12 months.

items.question: When does the warranty start?
answer: On the day your order is delivered, as shown in your tracking. It runs for 12 months from that date.

items.question: I received my piece as a gift. Am I covered?
answer: Yes. The warranty belongs to whoever wears the piece. Scan the QR code inside the box and register in your own name, and your coverage starts from the delivery date.

items.question: What does the one year warranty cover?
answer: Setting and prong failure, chain, clasp and link breakage caused by a manufacturing defect, metal defects such as cracks, breaks or casting flaws, and any structural failure caused by defective materials or workmanship.

items.question: What is not covered?
answer: Normal wear such as scratches, scuffs and patina. Loss or theft. Accidental damage such as a chipped stone or a bent band. Chemical exposure, including perfume, chlorine and saltwater. Improper storage or moisture damage. Repairs or alterations by anyone other than Difinery. Engraving that wears with time. Anything outside normal use.

items.question: How do I file a warranty claim?
answer: Email support@difinery.com with your order number, the name you registered under, or proof of purchase, clear photos of the issue, the date you noticed it and a short note on how the piece has been worn and cared for. We respond within 24 hours with next steps and a prepaid shipping label if one is needed. Inspection takes 3 to 5 business days, and an approved repair or replacement is completed and shipped back within 7 to 10 business days. If the design has been discontinued, we offer an equivalent replacement or a full refund.

items.question: What if I do not have my order number?
answer: Proof of purchase works in place of an order number. So does the email address used at checkout, or the name you registered under with the QR code. Send us whatever you have and we will find the order.

items.question: Who pays shipping for warranty claims, cleaning and out of warranty repairs?
answer: If we approve a claim as a manufacturing defect, Difinery covers shipping in both directions. For the complimentary cleaning and polishing service, we cover the leg back to you. For out of warranty repairs and for any service quoted and approved as paid work, shipping to us is the customer's responsibility, quoted plainly with no hidden fees.

items.question: Do you offer resizing?
answer: Most Difinery rings can be resized, and each includes one complimentary resizing within 60 days of delivery, with free return shipping back to you. Full eternity bands, where diamonds run all the way around, generally cannot be resized without being remade, so getting the size right at order matters more with those. If you are not sure whether your design can be resized, ask us before you order.

items.question: How do I request a resize?
answer: Email support@difinery.com with your order number and your new size. Ship the ring to us with a tracked and insured carrier. We resize within 10 to 14 business days and ship it back to you free and insured.

items.question: Can I resize again after the complimentary resize?
answer: Yes. Additional resizing is available at a fair cost, quoted before any work begins.

items.question: Do you repair pieces after the warranty ends?
answer: Yes. We offer polishing and cleaning, stone tightening, clasp replacement, chain and link repair, resizing, and metal refinishing and structural repair, all at a reasonable cost quoted in advance.

items.question: An accent diamond fell out after the warranty ended. What now?
answer: That is handled as a standard post warranty repair, which includes stone tightening and replacement. Send us photos and we will assess the piece and give you a detailed quote you can approve or decline. If you approve, you ship the piece to us at your cost and we handle the rest.

items.question: How do I get a repair estimate?
answer: Email us photos of the piece and a description of the issue. We assess the condition and send a detailed quote. You approve or decline it before anything happens. If you approve, you ship the piece to us, and shipping to us is your responsibility. No surprise charges are added afterward.

items.question: I lost a diamond and I am outside the warranty. Can you help?
answer: Yes, as a paid repair. Send photos and we will quote the replacement stone and the setting labor. This is also the case where jewelry insurance earns its keep, since a policy typically covers loss and accidental damage while a manufacturer's warranty covers defects.

items.question: What is included with my purchase?
answer: Every piece arrives in a plain outer shipping box with our signature Difinery presentation box inside, your piece in a linen jewelry case made to be kept and reused, a gift note card, and a QR code to register your one year warranty and extend your complimentary cleaning to 12 months. Center diamonds of one carat and above also include their IGI grading report. An appraisal is not included, and we can arrange an independent appraisal for $100 per piece if you need one for insurance.

items.question: Do your photos show the exact piece I will receive?
answer: Our photography accurately represents the design, materials and specifications of the piece you will receive, including the same style, metal, diamond shape and total carat weight. Because every piece is made to order and finished by hand, tiny natural variations exist between individual pieces, as they do with any handmade jewelry.

items.question: Do weights and dimensions change with size?
answer: Yes, especially for rings. A different ring size changes the amount of metal used and the final weight, and for some designs it changes the number or total weight of the accent diamonds. Specifications are listed for a reference size, usually size 6, and vary slightly at other sizes.

items.question: Can I engrave my piece?
answer: Yes, on rings, necklaces and bracelets, and engraving is complimentary. You can add up to 15 characters on rings and up to 10 on necklaces and bracelets, including spaces, such as initials, a date or a short word, in any font style you like. If a style or length would not come out clearly at that size, we will reach out before engraving and suggest an alternative. Please note that engraved pieces are personalized for you and are final sale.

items.question: Does engraving affect returns, resizing or the warranty?
answer: Engraved pieces are final sale and cannot be returned. Engraving does not affect your warranty, though engraving that wears down over years of use is considered normal wear rather than a defect. Resizing a ring can affect an engraving on the inside of the band depending on its placement, and we will tell you before we resize if that is the case.

items.question: Do you offer matching sets?
answer: Not as pre bundled sets. Every product page has a "pair it with" section featuring pieces chosen to work together, so you can build a set that suits you rather than buying one we assembled.

items.question: Can I include a gift note?
answer: Yes. Every order comes with a Difinery gift note card. Add your message in the notes field at checkout and we will write it out and tuck it in with your piece, so it is ready to give. Our presentation box needs no extra wrapping.

items.question: Do you sell gift cards?
answer: Yes. A Difinery gift card lets the recipient choose exactly what they want, which is often the smarter move for jewelry. Gift cards are delivered by email and do not expire.

items.question: How do I choose my first fine jewelry piece?
answer: Start with something that fits how you actually live. Decide whether you want it subtle or noticeable, whether it will be worn every day or occasionally, and which metal color you already reach for. A piece you wear constantly is worth more than a piece you admire in a drawer. If you want a second opinion, email support@difinery.com and we will give you an honest one.

items.question: How do I choose a jewelry gift?
answer: Watch what they already wear. Note the metal color, whether their taste runs delicate or bold, and whether they wear rings, necklaces, earrings or bracelets most. Necklaces and bracelets are the most forgiving to buy for someone else because sizing is flexible. If you are unsure, a gift card removes the guesswork entirely.

items.question: Can I mix yellow, white and rose gold?
answer: Yes. Mixing metals is a deliberate and well established styling choice, and some Difinery designs let you choose a different gold color per element. There is no rule against it and there never was.

items.question: How do I layer necklaces without tangling them?
answer: Space the lengths at least two inches apart, so a 16 inch with an 18 inch or 20 inch rather than two 16 inch chains. Mix a pendant with a plain or station chain rather than two pendants of similar size. And put them on in order, shortest first.

items.question: What jewelry works for everyday wear versus occasions?
answer: For everyday, look for low profile settings such as bezel and flush set stones, secure closures and pieces that will not catch on clothing. For occasions, higher settings, larger stones and more movement all read beautifully because you are not wearing them through a workday.

items.question: What is a solitaire ring?
answer: A ring with a single center diamond and no other stones on the band. Simple, timeless, and the design that keeps the focus entirely on the center stone.

items.question: What is a halo setting?
answer: A halo is a ring of small diamonds set closely around the center stone. It adds sparkle and makes the center stone look larger than it is.

items.question: What is a hidden halo?
answer: A ring of small diamonds set underneath the center stone, facing outward from the side rather than around the top. Invisible when you look straight down at the ring, and a flash of light from every other angle.

items.question: What is a prong setting?
answer: Metal claws that hold a diamond in place at its edges. Prongs let the most light into the stone, which maximizes sparkle, and they are the most common setting for a center diamond.

items.question: What is a bezel setting?
answer: A rim of metal that wraps the edge of a stone completely or partially. Bezels are the most protective setting, sit low on the finger and do not catch on clothing, which makes them a strong choice for everyday and active wear.

items.question: What is a pavé setting?
answer: Many small diamonds set closely together with tiny beads of metal, so the surface reads as continuous sparkle. The name comes from the French for paved.

items.question: What is a fishtail setting?
answer: A setting where the metal is cut and shaped around each stone into small V shapes, resembling a fishtail. It holds the stones securely while showing very little metal, which keeps the line of diamonds looking bright and continuous.

items.question: What is a channel setting?
answer: Stones set in a row between two parallel walls of metal, with no prongs between them. Very secure and very smooth, which is why it is popular for wedding bands.

items.question: What is a contoured wedding band?
answer: A band shaped with a curve or notch so it sits flush against an engagement ring, wrapping around the center stone instead of leaving a gap. Difinery makes contoured bands to order to fit your specific ring.

items.question: What is an eternity band, and what is the difference between full and half?
answer: An eternity band has diamonds set around the ring so it sparkles from every angle. A full eternity band carries stones all the way around. A half eternity band sets stones across the top portion only, with plain metal underneath. Half eternity bands are generally more comfortable, easier to resize and less prone to a stone being damaged against a desk or a steering wheel.

items.question: What is a statement ring?
answer: A bold, visually distinctive ring built to be noticed, usually through a larger stone, an unusual shape, a sculptural form or a dense cluster of diamonds.

items.question: What is a stackable ring?
answer: A ring designed to be worn alone or combined with others on the same finger. Vary the width, texture, shape or diamond detail to build a stack that feels balanced.

items.question: What is an open ring?
answer: A ring with a small gap rather than a closed circle, so the two ends sit near each other on the finger. The open shape reads modern and light. It is not adjustable, so choose your true size.

items.question: What is a three stone ring?
answer: A ring with a center diamond flanked by two side stones. It is often given meaning as past, present and future, and it is a popular engagement ring alternative to a solitaire.

items.question: What is a toi et moi ring?
answer: French for "you and me." A ring with two stones set side by side, usually of different shapes, representing two people. It is one of the oldest engagement ring forms and has come back strongly.

items.question: What is a signet ring?
answer: A ring with a flat or slightly domed face, traditionally engraved with initials or a crest. Historically used to seal documents, now worn as a personal piece, often on the pinky.

items.question: What is a diamond bracelet?
answer: Any bracelet featuring one or more diamonds, from a single accent stone to a continuous line of them, and anywhere from delicate to bold.

items.question: What is a tennis bracelet?
answer: A flexible bracelet with a continuous line of diamonds set in articulated links, so it moves with the wrist.

items.question: Why is it called a tennis bracelet?
answer: The name is associated with the tennis player Chris Evert, who lost a diamond bracelet during a match and asked for play to be paused while it was found. The style has been called a tennis bracelet ever since.

items.question: What is the difference between a tennis bracelet and a diamond bracelet?
answer: Diamond bracelet is the general category, covering any bracelet with diamonds. A tennis bracelet is one specific style within it, defined by a continuous line of diamonds, usually in a single row.

items.question: What is a tennis necklace?
answer: The same construction as a tennis bracelet, worn at the neck: a continuous line of diamonds in flexible links.

items.question: What is the difference between a pendant necklace and a station necklace?
answer: A pendant necklace has one central element hanging from the chain. A station necklace has multiple diamonds or decorative elements placed at intervals along the chain.

items.question: What are diamonds by the yard?
answer: Individual diamonds spaced evenly along a fine chain, usually separated by short sections of chain and often bezel set. It is a station style design.

items.question: Why are they called diamonds by the yard?
answer: The name describes how the diamonds are distributed along the length of the chain at intervals rather than gathered into one pendant. It does not mean the necklace is a yard long.

items.question: What are stud earrings?
answer: Earrings that sit directly on the earlobe, usually a single diamond, stone or metal element secured with a post and a backing.

items.question: What are hoop earrings?
answer: Circular or oval earrings that pass through the earlobe and form a continuous shape, from small and minimal to large and bold.

items.question: What are huggie earrings?
answer: Small hoops that sit close against the earlobe, so they hug the ear rather than hanging from it. Comfortable enough to sleep in and a good choice for a second or third piercing.

items.question: What is a baguette diamond?
answer: A long, rectangular step cut diamond with straight edges and clean lines. Baguettes read architectural rather than sparkly and are often used as accents or set in a row along a band.

items.question: What is a marquise diamond?
answer: An elongated shape with pointed ends, sometimes called a navette. It carries its weight across a large surface area, so it looks larger than its carat weight suggests and elongates the finger.

items.question: How do I contact Difinery?
answer: Two ways. Call us at +1 (212) 470-3049, Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm Eastern. Or email support@difinery.com and we respond within 24 hours.

items.question: Do you have a phone number I can call?
answer: Yes. +1 (212) 470-3049, Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm Eastern. If we miss you, leave a message and we will call you back.

items.question: Do you offer virtual consultations?
answer: Yes. You can book a video consultation on our website. It is the best way to see pieces at real scale, ask questions about diamonds and settings, and talk through a custom idea before committing.

items.question: How can press reach you?
answer: For press and media inquiries, email us at admin@difinery.com.

items.question: Do you work with wholesale or trade partners?
answer: For partnership and trade inquiries, email admin@difinery.com and we will get back to you within two business days.
